Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

safe adjective

out of danger; not dangerous

also safely, safer, in safety, keep safe, is it safe?, it’s safe to, safe from

classical

Caes. B.G. 7.14: ā perīculō (Lewis & Short)
Plaut. Most. 2.2.42: Tūtum probē est.
Traupman 373

tūtus, tūta, tūtum

adjective; safe from: ab + ablative · Declension on Wiktionary

safe, secure, out of danger

Safe from something is tūtus ab (ab hoste, Ov.). Also of a course that carries no risk: tūtum est with an infinitive, it is safe to (Quint. 9.2.66). In tūtō esse, to be in safety (Ter. Heaut. 4.3.30). Adverb tūtō, safely.

Other words

  • innoxius, innoxia, innoxium — harmless, not dangerous

    also used · classical · Plin. NH 8.229 (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. safe (Tac. H. 4.20: innoxium iter) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Of a thing or an animal that does no harm. Also “innocent, guiltless” and, passively, “unharmed” (Lewis & Short).

  • sēcūrus, sēcūra, sēcūrum — safe (of a place); classically, free from care

    also used · post-classical · Liv. 39.1 (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Classically free from care, untroubled (from sē- and cūra); “safe, secure” of a place is rare and later than Augustus (Lewis & Short). Prefer tūtus.

Examples

  • Tūtum probē est.

    It’s perfectly safe (no one’s listening).Plaut. Most. 2.2.42 (Lewis & Short)

  • quārē sollicitum potius aevum dūcitis quam rēgem mē creātis ictō foedere, quī vōs ab omnī tūtās praestem injūriā?

    why spend your lives in fear rather than make a pact and choose me king, to keep you safe from all harm?Phaedr. 1.31.7–9

See also security, safe, protect, risk, safe journey, safe.
